newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED COULD CLINCH TITLE WITH WIN AT LEICESTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED COULD CLINCH TITLE WITH WIN AT LEICESTER.

text.p: Manchester United could become English league champions for the fourth time in five seasons if they win at Leicester on Saturday and other results go their way.
Although United already have the title virtually sewn up, Arsenal, Liverpool and Newcastle still have a mathematical chance of catching them but the slim hopes of all three could end on Saturday.
United have 69 points and four matches to play, Arsenal 65 with two to play, Liverpool 64 with three to play and Newcastle 60 with four to play.
Arsenal face Newcastle at Highbury on Saturday afternoon while Liverpool play Tottenham at Anfield in an evening match.

If United were to win in the morning at Leicester, Arsenal would be out of the running even if they beat Newcastle. Newcastle would be out of contention if they lost, while both would be out of the chase if they drew.

If Liverpool then failed to beat Tottenham, the final challenge to United would be over and Alex Ferguson's men would win the title again and would be able to take a relatively relaxed view of their final three matches to be played in seven days from next Monday.
If United were to lose at Leicester the title race would remain open at least until Monday when United play relegation-threatened Middlesbrough.

Even if United do take the title on Saturday, Arsenal, Liverpool and Newcastle will still battle it out all the way for the runners-up spot which next season carries with it a place in the European Champions' League. Six teams are still embroiled in the fight to avoid the drop.
The future is looking particularly bleak for bottom-placed Nottingham Forest, who are likely to go down even if they beat Wimbledon at home on Saturday and Newcastle away on Sunday week.
Middlesbrough, who must play four matches in the next nine days starting at home against Aston Villa on Saturday, might have to play with defender Neil Cox in goal.
Their four senior 'keepers -- Mark Schwarzer, Ben Roberts, Ben Cole and Gary Walsh -- are all unfit and the premier league rejected the club's request to play an on-loan keeper.
Cox, a former Villa player said: "I've done it before at Scunthorpe, and I did 40 minutes in goal for Villa once."
Middlesbrough, who could yet become the first team in English history to win the F.A. Cup and be relegated in the same season, are, like Forest, on 33 points.
That puts them four behind Sunderland who currently occupy the remaining relegation spot.
Sunderland have nosedived with just two wins in their last 14 matches and even if they beat Everton at home on Saturday and Wimbledon away in their final match they may still go down.

Southampton (38 points from 36 matches), West Ham (38 from 35) and Coventry (38 from 36) are all hovering just above the relegation zone and although the Hammers have a game in hand they have the toughest run-in with matches against Sheffield Wednesday on Saturday, Newcastle (home) and Manchester United (away).
